newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels kill seven in attacks on villages.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels kill seven in attacks on villages.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed seven people in attacks on four villages in southwestern Algeria, an Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.
The killings during the past week in the province of Saida, 350 km (220 miles) southwest of Algiers, included a fireman who had his throat slit, El Watan said.
The deaths were in addition to a series of killings in and around Algiers.

Villagers in Tabainat hamlet, 50 km (30 miles) of Algiers, on Tuesday buried 14 villagers killed on Monday, most of them hacked to death by Moslem guerrillas. Moslem rebels seized five girls from homes in nearby Haouch Englise. They were found on Monday with their throats slit.
The killings followed Sunday's fifth anniversary of the cancellation of a general election that radical Islamists were poised to win.
About 300 people have died in attacks, mostly in Algiers and surrounding areas, in the past two months. More than 60,000 people had died in fighting in Algeria since 1992.
